rule: Imports, `require`, re-exports (`export *`, `export * as`) and workspace packages (package.json `exports`) resolve to the defining module; packages outside the scan are named as written (`node:http.createServer`, `zod.z.object`, medium). | module = the file's path below the scan root without extension and trailing `/index` (`src/chat` for src/chat/index.ts; basenames collide across directories): `src/app.f`, `src/app.C#m`, `#<init>`/`#<clinit>`/`#field` as in Java. | Vendored and third-party code (`external/`, `vendor/`, `third_party/`, `Pods/`) | Call on a receiver of **unknown type**: `recv.member`, using the LAST receiver segment (`self.client.get()` → `client.get`; `a.b.c()` → `b.c`). | **C1 Symbol identity.** Every definition has exactly one ID. Every reference to it uses that ID: a call in the defining file, through an import, a re-export, an alias or a `require` binding.
notes: `@acme/strutil` is a workspace package (packages/strutil/package.json `exports`: ./lib/main.js); main.js re-exports pad.js with `export *` and casing.js with `export * as casing`. Both resolve to the defining modules (`packages/strutil/lib/pad`, `packages/strutil/lib/casing`), not to the package name or the re-exporting file. `casing.upper(...)` is a namespace-object function -> direct. vendor/left.js is in scope (Decisions 2026-11-09) and judged like any other code. main.js only re-exports: no edges.
